title: Pediatric Autoimmune Thyroid Disease: Hashimoto, Graves and Antithyroid Therapies

steps.title: Autoantibody Hallmark of Hashimoto Thyroiditis

left.title: Serological Markers
points: Hallmark of juvenile chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis

right.title: Clinical Hallmark
points: Leading cause of acquired pediatric hypothyroidism
Decline in linear growth velocity before weight changes

steps.tx: Chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis is the leading cause of acquired hypothyroidism and goiter in children, diagnosed by elevated serum anti-thyroid peroxidase (anti-TPO) in > 90% and anti-thyroglobulin (anti-TG) antibodies. Clinical evaluation confirms **Hashimoto thyroiditis antibody serology** as the diagnostic cornerstone, identifying an indolent, firm, non-tender goiter with insidious linear growth slowing. Early serological identification prevents neurocognitive slowing and growth arrest.
steps.say: Hashimoto thyroiditis is the foremost cause of acquired juvenile hypothyroidism, verified by high anti-thyroid peroxidase and anti-thyroglobulin titers.

steps.title: Transient Hashitoxicosis Presentation

nodes.label:
Colloid Discharge
Preformed T4 and T3 surge

Spontaneous Euthyroidism
Resolves in weeks to months

steps.tx: Initial presentation of Hashimoto thyroiditis can feature transient mild hyperthyroidism (hashitoxicosis) due to inflammatory disruption of thyroid follicles, which spontaneously subsides in weeks to months without antithyroid drugs. Follicular architecture ruptures under cytotoxic autoimmune attack, producing the **Hashitoxicosis transient phase** by spilling stored thyroglobulin into circulation. Thionamides are unnecessary because autonomous hormone hyper-synthesis is absent.
steps.say: Transient thyrotoxicosis from follicular disruption during early Hashimoto thyroiditis resolves spontaneously within weeks without antithyroid drugs.

steps.title: Pathophysiology of Pediatric Graves Disease

vis.alt: Thyroid stimulating antibodies causing goitre, eye changes, tremor and skin changes in Graves disease.
vis.caption: Graves disease: receptor antibodies drive goitre, eye signs and tremor. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: Pediatric Graves disease is driven by autoantibodies that bind and stimulate the TSH receptor (TRAb / TSI), causing smooth diffuse vascular goiter, weight loss, heat intolerance, proptosis, and accelerated linear growth. Understanding **Pediatric Graves disease pathogenesis** highlights increased osteoclastic bone turnover that initially accelerates stature velocity while disproportionately advancing epiphyses. Incomplete closure and premature craniosynostosis represent critical risks in early childhood thyrotoxicosis.
steps.say: Pediatric Graves disease stems from thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulins driving diffuse vascular goiter, hypermetabolism, proptosis, and rapid linear growth.

steps.title: Methimazole as Sole First-Line Thionamide

vis.alt: Thyroid hormone synthesis in the follicular cell and where antithyroid drugs block it.
vis.caption: Hormone synthesis and the steps blocked by antithyroid drugs. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: Oral methimazole (0.2-0.5 mg/kg/day once daily, max 30 mg) is the sole recommended first-line antithyroid drug in children; propylthiouracil (PTU) is strictly black-box contraindicated due to fatal fulminant hepatic necrosis. Clinical guidelines establish **Methimazole as exclusive first-line thionamide** therapy, fostering adherence and blocking thyroid peroxidase iodination without hepatotoxic mitochondrial toxicity. PTU remains restricted solely to refractory maternal thyrotoxicosis in early pregnancy.
steps.say: Oral methimazole once daily is the exclusive first-line thionamide in children because propylthiouracil carries a black-box warning for fatal hepatic necrosis.

steps.title: Agranulocytosis Surveillance Protocol

left.title: Warning Symptoms
points: Severe painful sore throat or pharyngitis

steps.tx: Parents must be educated to stop methimazole immediately and obtain urgent absolute neutrophil count (ANC) if the child develops fever, sore throat, or mouth ulceration; agranulocytosis (ANC < 500/mm³) occurs in 0.3-0.5%. The strict **Agranulocytosis monitoring rule** dictates that routine baseline surveillance remains uninformative because idiosyncratic marrow suppression develops precipitously. Prompt drug withdrawal and broad-spectrum antimicrobial cover avert fatal neutropenic sepsis.
steps.say: Families must halt methimazole and seek emergency neutrophil counts immediately if a child develops sudden fever or a severe sore throat.

steps.title: Beta-Adrenergic Blockade for Symptom Relief

nodes.label:
Bridge to Methimazole
Euthyroid at 4 to 8 weeks

steps.tx: Propranolol (1-2 mg/kg/day divided TID) or atenolol provides immediate symptomatic relief of palpitations, tachycardia, and severe tremor until methimazole achieves euthyroid state at 4-8 weeks. Adjunctive **Beta-blocker symptom control** counters sympathetic hyper-responsiveness that accounts for debilitating sleep disruption, fine motor instability, and emotional lability in school-aged children. Beta-blockers are safely tapered and discontinued once free thyroxine levels normalize into reference range.
steps.say: Beta-blocker therapy provides swift symptomatic control of palpitations and tremor until methimazole restores normal thyroid hormone levels over four to eight weeks.

steps.title: Definitive Ablative and Surgical Interventions

left.title: Total Thyroidectomy
points: Preferred in children under 5 years of age
Risks include recurrent nerve injury and hypoparathyroidism

right.title: Radioiodine Ablation (131-I)
points: Reserved for older pediatric cohorts > 5-10 years

steps.tx: If medical remission is not achieved after 2-3 years of methimazole, definitive treatment options are total thyroidectomy or 131-I radioiodine ablation (doses > 150-200 microCi/g, preferably in children > 5-10 years). Selecting **Definitive Graves therapies (Radioactive iodine vs Surgery)** avoids subtotal surgery or low-dose radioiodine due to unacceptable recurrence rates. Lifelong oral levothyroxine replacement begins immediately following complete thyroid tissue ablation.
steps.say: Definitive therapy with total thyroidectomy or radioactive iodine ablation is indicated when prolonged thionamide therapy fails to induce permanent remission.

steps.title: Neonatal Graves Disease from Maternal TRAb

nodes.label:
Neonatal Thyrotoxicosis
Tachycardia, failure to thrive

Gradual Resolution
Resolves by 3-4 months as IgG clears

steps.tx: Transplacental passage of maternal TRAb causes transient neonatal thyrotoxicosis (fetal tachycardia, craniosynostosis, cardiac failure), treated with methimazole, Lugol iodine, and propranolol, resolving by 3-4 months as maternal IgG clears. Recognizing **Neonatal Graves disease pathophysiology** is crucial because high maternal receptor antibodies trigger autonomous hypersecretion despite maternal euthyroid status post-ablation. Aggressive multi-agent therapy prevents acute congestive heart failure and premature cranial suture closure.
steps.say: Maternal antibody transfer can cause severe neonatal thyrotoxicosis requiring urgent multi-agent therapy, resolving naturally as maternal antibodies decay.
